title: A network failure cached in the revalidation's page or search memo is reused as not found by a second source
goal: A candidate page or search that got no HTTP answer (status 0) is recorded per use as an HTTP error is, so a second source that leans on the cached failure gets search_lost's reason and its lines keep the offline stamp, not not found. Found by the SP-u5q37ds3 review: _http_error ignores status 0, so only the first use bumps provider.failures() (_tools/factdiff.py page_doc, search_urls, search_lost).

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import factdiff as f, provider; provider.document=lambda url,row=None,etag='',lastmod='': (provider._failed.__setitem__(0, provider._failed[0]+1), {'status':0,'text':'','error':'URLError: timed out','etag':'','lastmod':'','version':{},'final':url,'hops':[],'raw':''})[1]; u='https://example.com/cand'; f.page_doc(u,[]); n=provider.failures(); k=len(f._unanswered_uses); f.page_doc(u,[]); sys.exit(0 if f.search_lost(n,k) else 1)

notes: Merged from ST-ve4a5sgq “A search that answers 200 with no result list (a sign-in page, an error object) keeps the offline stamp, not not found” at the 2026-10-13 draft triage: factdiff.search_urls (:1227) reads only HTTP errors as unanswered, so a 200 sign-in page gives res=[] (false not-found) and a JSON list raises AttributeError; same function, search_lost memo and files as BG-gx5b2yhu, whose repro fails now. Its goal: factdiff.search_urls records a 200 search answer whose body is not the provider's result list (HTML, a JSON error object, a JSON list) as no answer, named in search_lost, so a line whose passage search leaned on it keeps the offline stamp; a JSON list body raises no AttributeError.
